cards.text: After this, Jesus crosses to the other side of the Sea of Galilee, also called the Sea of Tiberias. Same sea, two names, just like me with Papa and Dorin. And a large crowd is following Him.

cards.question: A large crowd follows Jesus across the Sea of Galilee. Why are they following Him?

answers.text: They saw His signs on the sick
He invited them to the mountain

cards.text: Jesus goes up on the mountain and sits down with His disciples. Meanwhile, the Jewish Feast of the Passover is near.
Then Jesus looks up and sees a large crowd coming toward Him. He turns to Philip, one of His disciples, and asks, “Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?”

cards.question: Jesus asks Philip where to buy bread for the crowd. He's asking to ___ Philip, because He already knows what He's about to do.

cards.text: So Philip does the math out loud, right there on the mountain. Friend, I can't even split one batch of cookies evenly without three tries and a recount.

cards.question: Philip figures two hundred denarii would buy every person in the crowd a small piece of bread.

cards.text: Then Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, speaks up. He's spotted a boy with some food.

cards.question: Andrew points out a boy with some food. What does the boy have?

answers.text: Five barley loaves and two small fish
Seven loaves and a few small fish
A handful of flour and some oil

cards.question: Andrew says the boy's food should be plenty for this crowd.

cards.text: Five loaves and two fish for a huge crowd, and Jesus doesn't call a committee meeting. “Have the people sit down,” He says.

cards.question: There's plenty of grass in that place, so the men sit down, about ___ thousand of them.
Jesus takes the loaves and the fish, gives thanks, and hands them out to everyone seated. How much does each person get?

cards.text: Everyone is full, and then Jesus gives His disciples a cleanup job. Friend, the second anybody says the word “cleanup,” I am suddenly VERY busy checking an oven timer.

cards.question: Once everyone is full, Jesus tells His disciples to gather the leftover pieces so that nothing will be ___.
The disciples fill twelve baskets with the leftover pieces.

cards.text: Twelve baskets of leftovers from five barley loaves. I've baked a LOT of batches, friend, and I have NEVER ended one with more than I started with.

cards.question: When the people see the sign Jesus performed, what do they start saying about Him?

answers.text: This is the Prophet who is to come
This is Elijah come back to them
This is a new teacher of the law

cards.text: Then Jesus realizes what this crowd is about to do. They're about to come and make Him king, by force.

cards.question: Jesus realizes the crowd is about to make Him king by force. What does He do?

answers.text: Withdraws to a mountain by Himself
Sends the crowd away to the villages
Lets them take Him to Jerusalem

cards.text: When evening comes, His disciples go down to the sea. They get into a boat and start across.

cards.question: The disciples get into a boat and start across the sea. Where are they heading?
When the disciples set out across the sea, Jesus is in the boat with them.

cards.text: It's already dark out there. I spent years in the dark in a junk drawer, friend, and at least nobody asked me to row.

cards.question: The disciples are rowing across the sea in the dark. What makes the trip rough?

answers.text: A strong wind stirs up the sea
Heavy rain starts filling the boat
A thick fog hides the shore

cards.text: They've rowed about three or four miles. Then they see Someone coming toward the boat.

cards.question: In the dark, the disciples see Jesus approaching their boat. He's ___ on the sea.
When the disciples see Jesus walking on the sea toward them, they stay calm.

cards.text: They see Jesus walking on the sea, and they're terrified. But Jesus speaks up: “It is I; do not be afraid.”

cards.question: Jesus tells His terrified disciples not to be afraid. What happens next?

answers.text: They take Him in and land at once
They row the rest of the night to land
They turn the boat back toward the crowd

cards.text: The boat's on shore, but keep that apron on, friend. This story is just getting started.

findings.problem: Discovery questions dominate the walkthrough. The earlier cards give no basis for reasoning out the answers on stop 1 cards 2, 7, 9, 12, 13, 16 and 18, or stop 2 cards 2 and 7. Several other choices are similarly under-set-up, so most choice cards are not informed guesses.

rule.text: **A few discovery questions are fine.** Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card retells the five loaves and two fish from John 6:9 as well as Jesus' command from John 6:10, but its citation covers only John 6:10.

rule.text: **Cite exactly what the card uses.** Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question does not stand on its own. 'That place' has no antecedent within the question, and 'the men' does not identify Jesus' crowd without relying on cards that are no longer visible.

rule.text: **Always give context in the question.** The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out five rather than four or three. The blank simply asks for a number from wording the walkthrough has not yet supplied.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup only says that Someone is approaching the boat. It gives no way to reason out whether Jesus is walking, rowing or sailing, so the blank asks for the unseen wording of the line rather than a meaning the baker can infer.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
